title: Teaching models what people want
lede: How do you train a model toward a goal you can judge but not write down?
body: The answer began outside language entirely. In 2017 researchers at OpenAI and DeepMind trained a reward model from human comparisons, asking which of two behaviours was better, and then optimised against it. By 2019 the same method was fine-tuning language models; by 2020 it produced summaries people preferred to human-written ones.

In 2022 InstructGPT applied it to instruction following. A 1.3-billion-parameter aligned model was preferred to the raw 175-billion one. That result is the key to this chapter: alignment does not add much knowledge. It steers and draws out what pretraining already put there. Anthropic then wrote the rules down as a constitution, and in 2023 DPO showed the whole reinforcement-learning loop could be replaced by a simple loss.
transition: By late 2022 the technique was mature. What it lacked was an audience.
